overall: The Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by meeting June 8 without timely notice and by posting an insufficiently specific July 13 notice, but not intentionally; other allegations were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: A June 8 meeting was held without notice posted 48 hours in advance, and the Commission proceeded despite knowing notice was late.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find—and the Commission concedes—that it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the late-notice June 8 violation was intentional under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: The Commission indisputably violated the Open Meeting Law, but we decline to find that the Commission's violation was intentional.

allegations.summary: The July 13 notice listed approval of minutes without identifying which meeting's minutes would be approved.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the notice for the Commission's July 13 meeting was insufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission intentionally concealed that June 8 minutes would be approved at the July 13 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: On these facts, we do not find that the Commission intentionally concealed the fact that it would approve the June 8 meeting minutes during its meeting on July 13.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a rescheduled Notice of Intent hearing lacked new notice to abutters; this is not an Open Meeting Law question.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation because this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Commission deliberated outside a posted meeting between July 13 and July 20 to prepare its response to the first complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence to the contrary, we credit a public body's account of the facts.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission did not adequately discuss its response to the first Open Meeting Law complaint at its July 20 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: This practice—where staff members received the complaint and prepared a draft response for the Commission's consideration and approval during a meeting—satisfied the Commission's obligations.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law
All Commission members to attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar within 90 days of receipt of the letter
remedy_passage: We order the Commission's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Commission that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. In addition, we order all members of the Board to attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by our office within ninety (90) days of the Board's receipt of this letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
